seo.title: Rabat Travel Guide 2026 | Kasbah Oudayas, Hassan Tower & Chellah | MoroccoTripMap
seo.description: Plan your trip to Rabat: Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower, Mohammed V Mausoleum, Chellah, medina, hotels and practical tips.
seo.og_description: Kasbah, Hassan Tower, mausoleum, Chellah and Atlantic capital calm.

hero_subtitle: Morocco’s capital of calm power: Kasbah of the Udayas, Hassan Tower, Mohammed V Mausoleum, Chellah ruins and Atlantic light — Rabat rewards slower walks than the imperial inland cities.

overview.title: Why Visit Rabat?
overview.p1: Rabat combines political capital, Atlantic coastline and layered history: Almohad walls, Andalusian gardens in the Kasbah of the Udayas, the unfinished Hassan Tower, the royal mausoleum and the Roman–medieval site of Chellah. It feels more ordered and greener than Marrakech or Fez.
overview.p2: Two to three days cover the Kasbah, Hassan complex, Chellah and the medina without rushing. Use Rabat as a calm base between Tangier and Casablanca or before heading inland.

places.title: Must-Visit Places in Rabat
places.subtitle: Kasbah, tower, mausoleum, Chellah and the stops that define the capital.

oudayas.title: Kasbah of the Udayas
oudayas.desc: Blue-and-white lanes, Andalusian gardens and views over the Bouregreg estuary.

hassan.title: Hassan Tower
hassan.desc: Unfinished Almohad minaret and vast esplanade of columns.

mausoleum.title: Mohammed V Mausoleum
mausoleum.desc: Royal mausoleum beside Hassan Tower — marble, zellige and guards.

chellah.title: Chellah
chellah.desc: Roman and medieval necropolis with storks and quiet gardens.

medina.title: Rabat Medina
medina.desc: Compact old city between the Kasbah and the modern centre.

gardens.title: Andalusian Gardens
gardens.desc: Shaded gardens inside the Kasbah of the Udayas.

beach.title: Rabat Beach & Corniche
beach.desc: Atlantic front below the Kasbah — walks and cafés.

marina.title: Bouregreg Marina
marina.desc: Modern waterfront with views toward Salé.

museum.title: Musée Mohammed VI
museum.desc: Modern and contemporary art museum in the capital.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Kasbah, Hassan complex and Chellah without rushing.

day1.title: Kasbah, Medina & Beach
day1.desc: Morning in the Kasbah and Andalusian Gardens, medina walk, late afternoon on the corniche.

day2.title: Hassan Tower & Mausoleum
day2.desc: Hassan Tower esplanade and Mohammed V Mausoleum, afternoon Chellah or museum.

day3.title: Chellah, Marina or Day Trip
day3.desc: Chellah if not done, Bouregreg marina, or Salé / Casablanca.

directory.title: Where to Stay in Rabat
directory.subtitle: Centre hotels, kasbah-area riads and practical bases near tram lines.

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Cafés
eat.subtitle: Kasbah views, centre tables and Atlantic simple fare.

ricks.title: Kasbah cafés
ricks.desc: Tea and light meals with estuary views.

sqala.title: Centre restaurants
sqala.desc: Moroccan and international menus in the modern centre.

mounia.title: Medina kitchens
mounia.desc: Simple tagines and grills in the old city.

cabestan.title: Corniche stops
cabestan.desc: Cafés and seafood along the seafront.

1.title: Walk the core
1.desc: Kasbah, medina and Hassan complex are walkable with short taxi hops. The tram helps for longer stretches.

2.title: Chellah needs a plan
2.desc: Slightly outside the centre — taxi or clear walking route. Check closing times.

3.title: Dress at the mausoleum
3.desc: Modest dress is expected inside the Mohammed V Mausoleum; follow staff guidance.

transport.title: Getting there
transport.desc: Airport RBA, ONCF trains (including high-speed links), and easy connections to Casablanca and Tangier.

bargain.title: Medina shopping
bargain.desc: Calmer than Fez or Marrakech; still bargain politely in tourist stalls.

water.title: Atlantic wind
water.desc: The coast can be breezy; bring a layer for evening corniche walks.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Rabat
daytrips.subtitle: Salé across the river, Casablanca by train, and longer runs toward the imperial cities.

rabat.title: Salé medina
rabat.desc: Cross the Bouregreg for a quieter medina, the Great Mosque area and a different Atlantic face — easy half-day on foot or by tram.

casablanca.title: Casablanca (train)
casablanca.desc: About an hour by train — Hassan II Mosque and the corniche work as a focused day if you leave early.

mohammedia.title: Kenitra & Mehdiya
mohammedia.desc: North along the coast — lagoon, beach and a calmer town rhythm if you want sea air without Casablanca’s scale.

azemmour.title: Meknes & Volubilis (longer day)
azemmour.desc: Possible as a long day by car or organised tour; better with an overnight if you want the ruins without rushing.

q1.question: How many days in Rabat?
q1.answer: Two full days cover Kasbah, Hassan complex and Chellah. Three allow the marina, museum or a short day trip.

q2.question: Is Rabat worth visiting vs Casablanca?
q2.answer: Yes if you want monuments, a calmer capital and Atlantic walks. Casablanca is more business and modern scale.

q3.question: Can I visit the Hassan Tower interior?
q3.answer: The tower exterior and esplanade are the visit; access to the interior is generally not for the public.

q4.question: Is the Kasbah free?
q4.answer: Walking the lanes is free; the museum and some spaces may charge. Gardens are part of the Kasbah visit.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start in the Kasbah lanes and Andalusian Gardens while the light is soft. Climb to the viewpoint over the Bouregreg estuary.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Walk the compact medina, then continue down to the beach and corniche for Atlantic air and a café stop.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Head to the Bouregreg marina for a modern waterfront stroll, or dine in the centre / Agdal.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Visit the Hassan Tower esplanade and the Mohammed V Mausoleum. Dress modestly for the mausoleum interior.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Taxi to Chellah for Roman and medieval ruins, gardens and storks — one of Rabat’s quietest major sites.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Return to the centre for a calm dinner; Rabat evenings are lower-key than Marrakech or Casablanca.
detailed_itinerary.day3_m: Morning — Musée Mohammed VI or free time
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: If open, visit the modern art museum, or revisit a favourite corner of the Kasbah without a fixed plan.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Cross to Salé for a short contrast, or take the train to Casablanca for the Hassan II Mosque if time allows.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: A final corniche or marina walk before continuing your trip north or south.
